metadata.title: Community Rice Plantation by the Garo Community
metadata.description:
Drill sowing and dibbling (making small holes in the ground for paddy seeds) is an age old practice in certain regions of Northeastern India. The indigenous rice cultivators “push down a pointed peg into the ground, put the seeds into the hole, and cover it with earth—it grows better thus.”

This is in complete contrast with how rice is cultivated in other part of the country. This variety of rice that is being cultivated is known as 'Chagring' in Garo language. This rice takes about 6 months time to mature and tastes absolutely delicious.
